transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

On Samsung fridge-freezers, code 22E typically indicates a fault with the evaporator fan motor in the freezer section. This is the fan that pushes cold air from the freezer coils up into the fridge compartment. If this fan isn't working properly, or if the airflow is blocked by ice buildup (often caused by a defrost system issue), you will get this error and the fridge side will become warm while the freezer may still be cold. While it could be a faulty fan motor or an internal ice blockage, there are simpler things to rule out first. The most common owner-fixable cause for poor cooling in the fridge section is restricted airflow due to packing. Please check the vents inside the fridge compartment (usually on the back wall). Are they blocked by food or tightly packed shelves, preventing air from flowing into the fridge? Or are they clear?
The vents aren't blocked by food. Airflow from them is very weak though, and there's a bit of frost around the vent at the top back of the fridge. Fridge temp is 9C.

This ice blocks the cold air from reaching the fridge section, which explains why it is warm (9°C) while the freezer may still feel cold. The 22E code suggests a fan or airflow fault, but often the fan is just spinning into a block of ice. 1. Switch the fridge off at the wall socket.
2. Remove all food and store it in cool bags with ice packs.
3. Place towels inside both compartments and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted (this can take up to 24 hours).
4. Dry everything thoroughly, close the doors, and switch it back on. Please let me know if you found a solid block of ice behind the rear freezer panel when you did this, or if there was very little/no ice at all.

I did the full defrost and the code cleared and the fridge cooled down properly, but 22E came back about 10 days later. I can't get the inner back panel off, so I couldn't see behind it. No burning smell or anything tripping, by the way. Is there anything else I can do?

The fact that the error cleared and cooling returned after a full defrost, only for the problem to return about 10 days later, suggests this is an automatic defect rather than a one-off blockage. The appliance is failing to run its internal defrost cycle properly, allowing ice to build up on the evaporator coils (behind that rear panel you can't reach) and choke the airflow. The most likely cause is a failed component in the defrost system: either the heater element has burned out, the bi-metal thermostat/sensor has stuck open so it never triggers the heater, or the control board isn't calling for a defrost. The 22E code often appears because the fan eventually hits ice or fails to spin freely. To confirm this is most likely the defrost system and not just the fan motor itself: run the fridge as normal with the doors shut for a few days (or up to a week). Has the frost started to build up again in the freezer compartment, or is it staying clear? If you see heavy ice building up again, that suggests the defrost system has failed. Because this involves internal components like the heater and thermostat which require dismantling the rear panel to access and test with a multimeter, this will need an engineer to replace the faulty part. If there is no frost build-up at all but you still get weak airflow, then it points more strongly to the evaporator fan motor itself being faulty. Please let me know what happens over the next few days.
